newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 23.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Unipetrol, a petrochemical holding company, is likely to make management changes in the coming weeks.
- The Czech National Bank's anti-inlfationary measures are beginning to make themselves felt by the decline in growth of M2 money.
- 1996 beer production in the Czech Republic is expected to increase to 18.2 million hectolitres, 300 thousand hectolitres over 1995's level.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka, which was the last of the large banks not to own shares in any pension fund, became a 10-percent shareholder in PF Energie.
PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel spent Saturday visiting Lidice in Brazil, a town named after the Czech village which was destroyed by the Nazis in 1944.

- Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda accused large banking houses with partial state ownership of adding to the current difficulties with Agrobanka by withdrawing funds from Agrobanka and by forming a sort of unofficial cartel.

- The executive committee of the Civic Democratic Party expressed support for Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik. They entrusted him with creating a legislative proposal for tightening up the supervision of the monetary and capital markets.
- Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said he would offer his resignation if the state budget will not be approved by Wednesday.

- Motoinvest is no longer the majority owner of Vojensky Otevreny Penzijni Fond, one of the two largest Czech pension funds. A group of industrial companies obtained the majority share in the last few days.
- Velkopopovicky Kozel beer was awarded first prize in the World Beer Championships, held annually in Chicago.
- Altogether 623.9 million crowns of the state budget were used for the support of entrepreneurialism this year.
- Ceska Pojistovna should also repay clients of the failed Kreditni Banka who had deposit certificates according to Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik.
